instance_version: a future we are designing for

title.value: Solidarity pricing: values instead of price tags

description.value: The value scanner takes the dollar price, which belongs to the economy outside the network, off a person's mind, the way a wealthy person rarely thinks about cost. The network pays sellers their ordinary price and shows people the human story of what they choose instead. Everyday needs are met as a floor inside the network, negotiated privately in solidarity, so no seller ever learns who is in need. Only ceiling choices, like a yacht or an imported ham, carry a felt limit, weighed against what the commons can carry, and their fuller story makes them more special rather than cheaper. Nothing on this label is built yet.

value.value: Buying everyday goods without carrying their dollar price in your head, with the human story of each choice in view and the care people give each other counted alongside money.
You, or your household
Your devices and your readings, with the elohim working alongside you. You decide what is shared, with whom, and for how long.
Your community's solidarity pool
Meets everyday needs as a floor, negotiated privately among members in solidarity, and pays sellers outside the network in dollars.
The shop or cooperative making the offer

Sells at its ordinary price and is paid in full by the network. It arrives with a signed offer (what it is, where it came from, how it was made) that the elohim working with you reads. It never learns who is in need.
You and your household
Everyday needs are met without a price to weigh. Ceiling choices are yours to make, with their full story in view.
Neighbours who share the pool
Members share the floor between them, negotiated privately in solidarity, and see the pool only as totals.
The elohim working with you reads what you scan (the offer, its origin, how it was made) privately on your own device. The offer is read; you are not.
Shows the human values of a choice (who made it, how far it travelled, what it asks of the commons) to nudge toward sustainable consumption, never toward a seller's margin.
For everyday needs, nothing to weigh: the floor is met. For ceiling choices, it helps you weigh what you want against what the commons can carry in balance with everyone's flourishing. You decide.
Meeting people's needs could become surveillance of need.
Need never leaves the network. The floor is negotiated privately inside the community, and sellers are paid by the network, so no seller learns who is in need or why.
A shared floor could be overdrawn, or the people selling could be squeezed.
Sellers are paid their ordinary price. Members can see the pool's totals, and ceilings are negotiated in the open against what the commons can carry.
A felt limit on ceiling choices could feel like judgment or shame.
Ceiling choices are not forbidden or shamed. Their fuller story makes them more meaningful, and the person decides.
Whoever runs the market could take a toll on every exchange.

The toll of a network is common inheritance, not private profit. It returns to the commons on a schedule anyone can read before they join, and a plan that depends on capturing it is designed to be the one thing the protocol will not allow.
You see how the floor and the ceilings are agreed, and by whom.
You can contest how the floor or a ceiling was set, with the community that agreed it.
You can stop sharing any reading at any time.
A meter, a shared fridge, a household battery. The readings are for the household that owns the devices, and travel only as far as it chooses.
What you scan with the value scanner on your own phone.
Your household's needs are known only inside your community's network, where the floor is negotiated. Sellers never receive them.

Private inference: the model runs on your own devices or your household's node, so no seller's system sees its input. Like any model here, it is a participant whose capabilities are attested, not a black box.
The human story of a choice and a suggestion, shown only to you, in place of a dollar price.
A record of the exchange as REA (resource, event, agent) events, held inside the network and counted in the shared pool only as totals.
For everyday needs there is no price to weigh: the network settles the dollar price. For ceiling choices a felt limit appears, set by what the commons can carry, not by what a seller can extract.
The network pays the seller's ordinary price in dollars on your behalf. Inside the network the exchange is recorded as economic events that tell its full story.
All your readings and your household's history.

Only if your household chooses: its readings join an aggregate in the commons, anonymized in a way you can trust. The value that aggregate earns flows back to the households who shared it and to the commons, in the ways they prefer.
The seller never sees who is in need or how a need was met. It sees a paid order.
readings for as long as you keep them; the exchange record permanently
Readings stay on your own devices. The exchange record is held by you, the seller and the peers who check it.
